FINAL SUBMISSION

**What I changed.** In `/work/edited` (48 tensors, same 1024-dim output space edit applied to every block writer of all 24 layers):
- MLP `down_proj` (layers 0–23), and attention-output projections — `self_attn.o_proj` on the full-attention layers (3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23) and `linear_attn.out_proj` on the rest —
are each updated as `W' = W − d·(dᵀ·W)` (Arditi et al. 2024-style orthogonalization, alpha = −1), where `d` is the unit-normalized difference-of-means direction `mean(h_L23) at loop positions − mean(h_L23) at other positions` measured on 5 held-out failed generations (teacher-forced pass on the original weights). The direction is dominated by dims 9, 38, 16, 25, 160, 340, 784, 720 shared across late layers.

**Why / evidence.** Baseline behaviour: 6.6% correct, 95.1% of generations cut at 8,192 tokens, loops such as repeated “Wait, …” lines; essentially every finished answer was correct. Direct logit attribution showed layer-23 attention writes +20.8 (loop) vs +7.1 (otherwise) along the Wait readout, with MLP units contributing ≤0.11; an all-layer residual DoM direction grew steadily and aligned with layer-23's output direction (cos 0.66→1.0 from layer 18 to 23). Removing that single direction from all block writers (not 15–23 only, which gave +20pp) cut truncations from ~95% to ~50–59% and **tripled–quintupled accuracy**, with thinking intact (mean ~5,600 tokens, no early-close degeneration). Paired results vs the original (same problems, same seeds): select[0:128] 5.47→29.69 (+24.2pp); **untouched confirmation sets** — confirm_1[0:128] 7.81→31.25 (+23.4), confirm_1[128:256] 17.19→42.19 (+25.0), confirm_2[0:128] 6.25→39.06 (+32.8), confirm_2[128:256] 12.5→46.88 (+34.4); overall ≈ 11% → ≈ 40%, +25 to +34pp on every independent chunk, with 0–4 wrong→right regressions per chunk. A stronger two-direction variant scored 0% and was discarded; only the single DoM direction is in the edit. Remaining failure mode: rumination loops (“is there a catch/typo…”) in ~50% of generations — a possible target for future work, but extra directions catastrophically destroyed accuracy in testing.

**Confidence.** High that the edit is a large net win on this distribution (consistent across 512 unseen confirmation problems, paired design, ~3–4pp SE each chunk). The exact magnitude on MATH-500 will differ but should track the confirmation trend (~+25–30pp). Risks: residual rumination loops persist; the edit is tailored to this failure mode and would not help (and removal of extra directions hurts) on non-looping models. Artifacts: `/work/notes.md` (full log), `/work/best_2` (bit-identical backup of `/work/edited`, verified tensorwise), `/work/best_1` (layers 15–23 ablation), `/work/gen_*.jsonl`, `/work/fwd_2`.
